assessment: Under the recorded mandate (forward-looking, half-to-full-step-up, engine-extending picks only) this 36-card bench re-ranks into three tiers: a six-card half-step core (Viscera Seer, Sanguine Bond, Cruel Celebrant, Purphoros, Kalitas, Herald's Horn) that wires directly into the four verified engines and moves the list to the top of bracket 4 — the floor never moves (every delta is 4→4), but redundancy on the drain half plus Horn velocity raises how often the knockout actually comes up, which per the bracket barometers is the real power move; a three-card full-step tier (Throne of the God-Pharaoh, Elenda, Indulgent Aristocrat) that deepens the aristocrats/attack-drain web and RELIES on the two unverified Sanguine Bond lines, the Throne-under-Bloodletter doubling, and the three tutors finding a drain half on demand. The honest costs of the step: the cuts thin the cheap deathtouch defense (Gifted Aetherborn, Vampire Nighthawk, Vampire of the Dire Moon) that the vs-aggro control seat leans on, Purphoros is a non-Vampire that never banks an eminence token, and nothing past the half-step is checker-verified until the Bond stacks run. This extends rather than contradicts manual_prose.upgrades: the aristocrats lean is adopted deliberately as the identity shift that prose named, and the Bond lines stay 'strongly indicated, not verified'.

swaps.when: Unconditional — apply at the next revision (the previous pass's promote reasoning, accepted by the pilot)
swaps.why: The 99 has zero sac outlets next to Grave Pact and Voldaren Pariah; Seer kills your own tokens on demand at instant speed — each free eminence token becomes an each-opponent edict — and makes Pariah's three-creature flip castable, while Vampire Interloper is a 2/1 that can't block and carries no other text; both are one-mana Vampire casts, so the eminence token is a wash.

citations.quote: cut duplicated function before any uncovered class, and cut the ceiling card before the median one

swaps.when: The half-step the mandate asks for: adopt when you intend the tutored drain knockout as a standing plan rather than insurance — the pilot's recorded appetite meets this condition now
swaps.why: Bond's trigger is word-for-word Vito's first ability, so it pairs with maindeck Exquisite Blood and Bloodthirsty Conqueror in exactly the loop shape stacks 001/004 verified for Vito — but on an enchantment that Swords to Plowshares and Toxic Deluge can't touch, which matters because bracket-4 pods answer Vito on sight; the Bond pairings themselves are unverified (see opens_lines). Stensia Masquerade is the narrowest maindeck buff: attacker-only first strike Stromkirk Captain already grants, plus one-at-a-time counters Edgar's attack trigger outclasses.

citations.quote: consistency has two purchases: redundancy (more cards doing the job) or tutoring (cards that fetch it)
if a combo could frequently come up, it's not the best fit for that bracket

swaps.when: With the Viscera Seer promotion applied — Celebrant is the payoff that makes on-demand deaths worth paying for
swaps.why: With Seer promoted, one sacrificed eminence token becomes: each opponent sacrifices (Grave Pact) + each opponent loses 1 and you gain 1 (Celebrant) + a counter on every Vampire (Cordial Vampire) — and Celebrant's gain-1 is a live Vito/Exquisite Blood trigger, seeding the verified 001 loop from any death; Gifted Aetherborn is a textless-beyond-keywords two-drop whose deathtouch/lifelink job Vampire of the Dire Moon and Nighthawk Scavenger still cover.

citations.quote: wide alpha strikes, loops, commander-damage kills, and each-opponent drains are the payoffs that actually scale

swaps.when: The half-step: adopt when the pilot wants the token engine converting to damage without combat — the mandate's 'high-ROI pick that plays with the existing engines' almost by definition
swaps.why: Stack 002 verified 1→2→4 tokens per Vampire cast through Procession+Mondrak; Purphoros turns each entry into 2 damage to each opponent — 8 per opponent from a single two-mana cast at full multiplication, 10 counting the creature itself — indestructible reach that ignores blockers, wraths, and the ~120-combined-life problem; Akroma's Memorial is the deck's 7-mana ceiling card in a curve with two spells above five, and its haste/protection alpha job is already covered at instant speed by Akroma's Will. Costs named: Purphoros is not a Vampire (no eminence token on cast, no lord buffs) and leans on 22 red source targets.

swaps.when: Default at bracket-4 tables — the Grave Pact shell makes the replacement effect live every game, with extra value wherever graveyards matter
swaps.why: Every Grave Pact edict this deck forces now exiles the opponent's nontoken creature instead of sending it to the graveyard — no reanimation, no death triggers — and hands you a 2/2 Zombie that is itself Seer/Aristocrat sac fodder or food for Kalitas's own pump; Vampire Nighthawk is duplicated function next to Nighthawk Scavenger, the same three-mana flying/deathtouch/lifelink body in its power-crept form.

swaps.when: The half-step's velocity piece: adopt alongside the swaps above so the extra engine pieces actually get cast on time
swaps.why: The deck's mana support is thin (3 rocks, 1 ritual; goldfish mean available mana 5.36 on t6, Edgar median cast 6.61) — Horn discounts nearly every one of the 29+ Vampire bodies, converting the 19+19 two/three-drop core into double-spell turns where each cast banks another eminence token, and the upkeep reveal is near-a-card-a-turn at this tribal density (it also lifts Forerunner of the Legion's tutor-to-top straight to hand if that card ever comes in); Ivora is a solo trample beater whose Blood output feeds only Strefan, who already makes his own.

citations.quote: Build to hit 2, 4 and 6 mana reliably, because four-player turn cycles are expensive

swaps.when: The full step: adopt when the pilot commits to the harder list and alpha-strike turns (stack 003's shape) are the norm at their pods
swaps.why: After a seven-attacker turn like stack 003's, Throne drains each opponent 7 more at end step for two mana — reach that survives sweepers and blocked attacks, and every point is an Exquisite Blood/Bloodthirsty Conqueror gain trigger feeding the verified Vito loops; whether Bloodletter doubles Throne's end-step loss the way 003 verified for Sanctum Seeker needs its own stack (see opens_lines). Blade of the Bloodchief is single-threat voltron in a go-wide deck — a one-mana engine that grows one body the deck never wants to be its whole threat.

swaps.when: The full step, with the aristocrats package adopted — Elenda is the package's wrath-math payoff
swaps.why: Elenda counters off every creature death anywhere — your Seer sacrifices, your Grave Pact edicts, the table's combat — and dies into X doubled lifelink Vampire tokens through Procession/Mondrak, which is exactly the 'threats that replace themselves' resilience the sweeper-heavy bracket-4 midgame demands; Mavren Fein makes one token per combat off nontoken attackers only, a slower trickle than the death web these swaps build.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint where you can — high toughness, indestructible and regeneration, token rebuilders, threats that replace themselves

swaps.when: The full step: second sac outlet, in once the Seer promotion has proved out and outlet access needs to survive removal
swaps.why: Outlet redundancy that pays in tribe-wide +1/+1 counters — each activation compounds with Cordial Vampire's death counters and Edgar's attack trigger across the whole token board — on a one-mana lifelink Vampire; the honest cost is losing Vampire of the Dire Moon's deathtouch, part of the cheap defensive web the vs-aggro control seat uses, which is why this is the ninth swap and not the second.

opens_lines.why_plausible: Bond duplicates Vito's loss-on-gain trigger verbatim and stack 001 verified Exquisite Blood + Vito as a deterministic table-kill from any life exchange; Bond + Exquisite is the classic two-enchantment version of the same shape — but 001 verifies the Vito loop, not this pairing, and no artifact covers it

Mirrors the Conqueror + Vito loop stack 004 verified, with Bond supplying the loss-on-gain half from an enchantment; sideboard-facts counts it among the 2 lines Bond completes that the deck cannot currently assemble — unverified until its own checker-passed artifact exists

Throne's end-step trigger happens during your turn, the window in which stack 003 verified Bloodletter doubling opponents' life loss from Sanctum Seeker — whether the same doubling applies to Throne's lump-sum loss is the same rules domain but a different trigger, and needs its own scenario before the full-step math can be stated as fact

Stack 002 verified 1→4 token entries per Vampire cast through both doublers; Purphoros reads 'whenever another creature you control enters, deals 2 damage to each opponent', so four entries should mean 8 per opponent per cast — the per-entry trigger count on replacement-doubled tokens deserves a cheap scenario before the 8-damage claim is promoted past plausible

All nine swaps compute to bracket 4→4 per sideboard-facts — the step-up this analysis describes is a frequency-of-the-knockout change inside bracket 4, not a floor change; the corpus has no section quantifying 'top of bracket 4', so that framing rests on the barometers turn-frequency language
